overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the unlisted clerk-consolidation vote was permitted, and the misrepresentation and bylaw claims fell outside OML review. Only non-binding encouragement was given.

allegations.summary: Board's vote to consolidate two clerk positions was allegedly not in the January 10, 2011 notice, which listed only 'Town Administrator's Report'.
allegations.key_passage: The Law does not require the chair to guess as to which topics members of the Board may discuss during a meeting.

allegations.summary: Town Administrator allegedly misrepresented facts by having the Board's secretary call the Personnel Board chair to keep him from the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: This office makes no finding as to this accusation, as it does not allege a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Consolidation of the two positions allegedly violated Town personnel bylaws.
allegations.key_passage: The Attorney General's Division of Open Government only has jurisdiction to enforce and interpret the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

source.publisher_filename: DETERMINATION - 6 8 2011 - OML 2011-23 - LEICESTER BOARD OF SELECTMEN.pdf
